opening_analysis.diagnosis: The opening is strong: it immediately states the core claim (Trinity ↔ Mathematical Structure) and the key result (Spirit as commutator). It pulls the reader in with a bold, specific assertion. The problem (the need to map theology onto formal structures) is implicit but clear. The opening could be improved by briefly stating why this mapping matters or what gap it fills.

unresolved_tensions: The tension between the strong claim of isomorphism and the acknowledged strains (e.g., personal/impersonal gap in ISO-006, self-grounding strain in ISO-007) is noted but not fully resolved.

missing_bridges: Between ISO-001 and ISO-002: a brief transition explaining the shift from mathematical structure to impossibility theorems would help.
Between ISO-005 and ISO-006: the shift from economics to information theory is abrupt.
redundant_passages: The 'NOT claimed' section is repeated in every ISO entry, which becomes redundant. Consider moving it to a single introductory note.
flow.suggested_reorder: The current order (by ISO number) is logical. No reordering needed.

paragraph_function_map.main_point: The Trinity maps onto a three-fold mathematical structure where the Spirit is the commutator of Father and Son.
The mapping is tested, bidirectional, and high confidence.
The mathematical domain is defined by information field χ with self-reference and conservation.
The theological domain is defined by the Trinitarian persons: Father, Son, Spirit.
Both domains share the structure: Generate → Structure → Actualize.
The mapping is not claiming God is a math equation or that the Trinity is reducible to logic.
The swap test confirms roles are non-interchangeable.
Predictions in physics: any complete theory needs all three modes; GR/QM tension may be an actualization bridge failure.
Predictions in theology: heresies map to mathematical pathologies; Filioque has a stronger mathematical analog.
Falsification conditions: find a complete system operating in only two modes, or show Trinitarian roles are interchangeable.
The isomorphism is high confidence at the axiomatic level.
Six impossibility theorems invert to produce a five-property specification that maps onto Pauline grace.
The mapping is tested, bidirectional, and high confidence.
The mathematical domain is defined by six impossibility theorems (Gödel, Tarski, Turing, Clausius, Landauer, Leibniz).
The theological domain is defined by five properties of grace from Ephesians 2:8-9.
Both domains describe systems structurally incapable of self-rescue, with the five properties being logical inversions of the impossibility theorems.
The mapping is not claiming grace is a theorem or that this proves Christianity true.
The swap test confirms one-to-one mapping between each property and a specific theorem.
Predictions in math/physics: no closed formal system will validate its own consistency; no self-contained AI can verify its own alignment.
Predictions in theology: Pelagianism is structurally incoherent; any coherent soteriology must have all five G-properties.
